title: The generic rigidity conjecture for k-triangulations
statement: A **$k$-triangulation** is a maximal set of pairwise noncrossing diagonals of a convex polygon in which no $k+1$ diagonals mutually cross. A graph is **generically minimally rigid in dimension $d$** if a generic embedding of its vertices in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space is minimally rigid. **Generic rigidity conjecture.** Every $k$-triangulation is generically minimally rigid in dimension $2k$. The conjecture extends the Laman characterization of generic minimal rigidity in the plane; the paper proves it for $k=2$, while the general case remains open.
source_name: Vincent Pilaud and Francisco Santos, “Multi-triangulations as complexes of star polygons”, arXiv:0706.3121 (2007).
